q: The central limit theorem says that with a big sample, the data become normal.
why: Myth. The sample MEAN becomes roughly normal. The data keep their own shape.

q: The sample size goes from 25 to 100. What happens to the standard error of the mean?
why: SE = σ/√n, and √100/√25 = 2. Four times the data only halves the error.

q: A bigger sample gives a sample mean that is, on average, closer to the true mean.
why: The standard error σ/√n falls as n grows. Any single sample can still be unlucky.

o: Highs and lows partly cancel out
why: One extreme value is diluted by the others in the average.
